name: Archaeological Sites of Mycenae and Tiryns
description: In Greece's Argolis region of the Peloponnese, Mycenae and Tiryns are the hilltop strongholds of the Bronze Age Mycenaeans, who ruled the eastern Mediterranean from about 1400 to 1200 BC. Tiryns, 20 km south of Mycenae, is known for its massive stone walls and the palace hall with its central hearth. Both cities are tied to Homer's epics and to the legend of Heracles.
